brief: Resilient growth and cautious investor positioning suggest equities can absorb more pressure before the rally is threatened, even as risks build: poor seasonality, oil above $100 pushing stocks and yields, looming Fed hikes, and AI executives calling for slower model development. Investors cut risk ahead of last week's hot inflation print and now face the Fed's rate decision Wednesday and a $2 trillion Triple Witching options and futures expiry Friday. SpotGamma says institutions are paying up for event protection through large out-of-the-money VIX call hedging. A Fed hold could ease yield pressure and clear volatility, while a hike could worsen bond volatility and stock pressure. Swaps now price 94% hike odds versus 60% a week earlier, with two more hikes expected by April. JPMorgan calls a shallow hiking cycle manageable, with a broader cycle and bigger equity downside not its base case. AI capex jitters look like a valuation shock, not a demand collapse per Saxo, whose warning signs would be capex cuts or canceled data centers. Goldman flags heavy short-driven CPI hedging last week. Deutsche Bank sees discretionary positioning underweight while systematic exposure hits an 11-month high, and argues absorbed catalysts open a rally window before midterm noise.
